prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1064; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Loss reported by the insured driver, who is named on the policy, after a low-speed collision in a parking lot. The claimant is represented by counsel, and the file was opened with the vehicle and the claimant both identified.

Entry 2: Police report and people present at the scene place the claimant in the vehicle at the time of impact. Photos taken at the scene show some details of the contact, but no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 3: Repair estimate reviewed. Most of the damage lines up with the impact described, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspections.

Entry 4: Claimant's counsel submitted a statement describing neck and back strain following the collision. The reported injury is plausible for a crash of this type, and the claimant has told the same account in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Medical records received. Treatment followed a usual course, with care tapering off as the claimant improved. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records provided.

Entry 6: Checked coverage history. Nothing suggests the damage happened before the policy coverage started, and the driver is confirmed on the policy as a listed driver.

Entry 7: File reviewed with the supervisor. Liability and injury components are being evaluated on the available evidence, and the next step is to request the final treatment summary from counsel.
